title: Professor Pudding and the Runaway Equation
author: StoryGen Community
markdown:
Professor Pudding was the most absent-minded mathematician in all of Numberton. She wore odd socks, kept biscuits in her pencil case, and once tried to water her calculator thinking it was a plant.

But today, something truly extraordinary had happened. One of her equations had come alive.

It started at half past nine, when she wrote **2 + 3 = ?** on the blackboard. The question mark wiggled. Then it jiggled. Then it leapt right off the board and bounced across the classroom floor.

"Oh my!" gasped Professor Pudding, dropping her chalk. "Come back here at once!"

But the little question mark was fast. It bounced out the door, down the corridor, and into the playground, leaving a trail of tiny ink spots behind it.

The children watched it go, eyes wide and mouths open.

"After it!" cried Professor Pudding, and off they all ran.

They chased the question mark through the school garden (where it hid among the question-shaped runner beans), past the library (where it tried to sneak into a mystery novel), and all the way to the park.

Finally, little Tomás had an idea. He held up a card with the number **5** written on it.

"Is this what you're looking for?" he called.

The question mark stopped bouncing. It tilted to one side, as if thinking, and then slowly floated back and settled into the equation on the blackboard, which now read:

**2 + 3 = 5**

"Well done, Tomás!" beamed Professor Pudding. "Every question just wants an answer."

And from that day on, the children in Numberton were never afraid of maths again — because they knew that every question mark was simply waiting for someone brave enough to solve it.
characters: Professor Pudding, Tomás, the children of Numberton
